hints.title: Aggregating by Value Occurrence
hints.text: Some email entries appear multiple times while others are unique. How can you group identical string values together and filter for only those groups that appear with a frequency greater than one?

hints.title: Grouped Count Invariant
hints.text: Grouping by a field combines identical values into singular buckets. Filtering aggregated group sizes requires a post-aggregation filter condition rather than a row-level filter.

hints.title: Group By with Having Filter Procedure
hints.text: Group the Person records by email. Apply a having clause specifying that the count of records in each email bucket exceeds one, and project the email attribute.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT email AS Email
FROM Person
GROUP BY email
HAVING COUNT(email) > 1;
```

complexity.notes: Single pass hash or index grouping with having count filter.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Cross joins or correlated subqueries checking for another record with the same email take O(N^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Group by with having processes all rows in O(N) time with O(U) auxiliary space for group counts.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Distinguishing between where and having clauses; understanding post-aggregation filter semantics.

solutions.code:
SELECT email AS Email
FROM Person
GROUP BY email
HAVING COUNT(email) > 1;
